text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, visiting Paris yesterday, was reassured that the French government will back Portugal's entry on its own merits to the first wave of Economic and Monetary Union.
- Angola could launch a national unity government on March 20, an observer of the transition process told the paper.
- Renault workers in Portugal will decide tomorrow whether to join a one-hour stoppage of colleagues in Spain, France and Belgium set for Friday.

- German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and former EU Commission president Jacques Delors have pressed former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez to replace Jacques Santer in the European Commission presidency, the paper says.

- Agriculture Minister Fernando Gomes da Silva sent a document to Brussels to renegotiate problems caused by the Common Agriculture Policy for Portuguese agriculture, notably a cut in support for cereal production, the paper learned.
- The government will change the way it calculates tax on cigarettes, which will reduce the tax burden on tobacco companies, the paper learned.
- The Bank of Portugal is revising upwards its estimate for Gross Domestic Product growth in 1996, which should stand at between 2.8 and 3.0 percent.
